     - Lingoda: the cited Lingoda article says `Founded 2012 (as Easy Languages), 2013 (as Lingoda)` in the infobox and says Lingoda is a Berlin-based language learning platform founded in 2012 by Fabian and Felix Wunderlich in the lead (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingoda`, lines 123-139). OpenClassrooms' own article describes it as a France-based online education platform, says it was founded in 2013 by Pierre Dubuc and Mathieu Nebra, and describes active online courses/memberships (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenClassrooms`, lines 142-168).
   - Additional Wiki-family challenge evidence: Unacademy has an English Wikipedia article, is an educational technology company providing an online educational platform with online courses and exam-prep materials, and was founded in 2015 (`https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unacademy`, lines 112-164). The current source set proves the 23 selected platforms have articles, but it does not define `the major B2C online learning platforms`; the direct MOOC list and nearby English Wikipedia platform pages materially change the row universe.
   - Minimal repair: choose a reproducible universe rule. Two defensible options are: (a) narrow the instance to `notable MOOC providers from List_of_MOOC_providers founded 2000-2020 and currently operating`, cite that list, and rebuild the rows; or (b) keep a broader B2C EdTech scope but add explicit list/source discovery rules and include/exclude all discovered in-scope English Wikipedia platform pages with a documented boundary.
